title: Variable dose-response relationship between exercise training and performance
population: Six previously untrained volunteers on a 15-week endurance training programme (8 weeks at 3 sessions/week, 4 weeks at 5 sessions/week, remaining weeks without training); performance = average power in a 5-min all-out exercise measured 3 times per week
findings: A nonlinear model was proposed with a variable accounting for training-related changes in the magnitude and duration of exercise-induced fatigue.
Standard error of fit was 6.47 +/- 0.71 W for the proposed model versus 9.20 +/- 2.27 W to 10.31 +/- 1.56 W for earlier models; the proposed model fitted significantly better in each subject.
The training programme produced a 30 +/- 7% improvement in performance.
The data demonstrated an inverted-U relationship between daily amount of training and performance.
limitations: Six untrained subjects on a cycle protocol. The comparison is goodness-of-fit, not out-of-sample prediction; a better fit with more parameters is not evidence of better prediction (see marchal-2025-ffm-statistical-flaws, busso-2023-impulse-response-validity). Re-classified from experimental-crossover to modelling: it is a single-group training study used to fit models, not a crossover.
implications: Offer the variable dose-response model (fatigue gain depends on recent load) only as an optional variant behind a forward cross-validation gate; keep the simple Banister form as the default when data are sparse.
Because the dose-response is inverted-U, cap modelled benefit of additional load; the optimiser must never recommend unbounded load increases.

verification.notes: Crossref confirms title, MSSE, 2003, single author Busso. All numbers match the Europe PMC abstract. Design corrected from experimental-crossover to modelling.
